prompt: The table below shows average weekly hours spent on three leisure activities by adults in a single country in 2000 and 2023. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
modelAnswer:
The table compares the average weekly hours adults spent on three leisure activities in 2000 and 2023. Overall, time spent online rose dramatically, while both television viewing and reading declined over the period.

In 2000, watching television was by far the most popular activity, taking up twelve hours a week, more than twice the time spent reading and six times that spent online. By 2023, this pattern had reversed almost entirely: online activities had grown sevenfold to fourteen hours a week, overtaking television, which fell to just seven hours. Reading also decreased, though less sharply, from five hours to three.

Overall, the data reveal a clear shift in leisure habits, with online activity replacing television as the dominant use of adults' free time, while traditional reading continued a slower decline.

prompt: Some people believe that children should begin learning a foreign language as early as possible, while others think it is better to wait until secondary school. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Write at least 250 words.
modelAnswer:
The question of when children should start learning a foreign language divides educators and parents alike, and both early and later approaches have credible support.

Those who favour an early start point to research suggesting that young children acquire new sounds and grammar more naturally than older learners, since their brains are especially adaptable during early childhood. Early exposure can also build confidence, as young children are typically less self-conscious about making mistakes than teenagers.

On the other hand, supporters of a later start argue that secondary school students can draw on stronger literacy skills in their first language, which helps them understand grammar rules more quickly. They also note that younger children have limited attention spans, so structured language lessons may be less effective than informal exposure through songs or games.

In my view, an early start is preferable, provided the teaching method suits young learners. Rather than formal grammar instruction, primary schools should use songs, stories and games to build familiarity with a language, reserving more structured grammar teaching for secondary school. This combined approach captures the cognitive advantages of an early start while respecting how young children actually learn best.

In conclusion, while both early and later introductions to language learning have merit, I believe an early, play-based start followed by more formal study later offers the best balance for most children.
